A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmegAMP and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–L. Content can be matched across the journal reformatting, relocations, and added studies.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation and classification experiments, plus antimicrobial assays of 25 designed peptides against 17 bacterial strains.

after.justification: v3 retains these original computational and experimental results and adds training-data, embedding, conditioning, and label-noise studies.

M1.justification: The diffusion UNet, five-scale embedding, PC/SC conditioning, synthetic-negative construction, and weighted XGBoost filtering are retained. Explicit embedding notation clarifies the reconstruction loss; stopping decoding at PAD was already documented in v2 Appendix B.2.2.

E1.justification: Appendix I.2 adds an auxiliary task predicting five physicochemical properties from peptide embeddings using existing AMP sequences. The peptide databases and bacterial species/strain coverage are otherwise retained; the AMP-only training experiment is an ablation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 12 introduces direct comparisons against PCA-reduced and average-pooled ESM-2 embeddings. The comparator sets in the existing generator, classifier, external-dataset, and experimental-success comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include AMP-only generator training, fivefold property-regression evaluation, a 42-pair conditioning grid with 250 sequences per pair, PC sampling over SC-derived ranges, and controlled positive-label corruption. These substantially expand controlled evaluation without revising the existing primary experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendices I.1, I.2, I.4, I.5, and J.3 add analyses of general-peptide training contributions, embedding informativeness, joint-property control, conditioning-range effects, and robustness to mislabelling. The earlier embedding, synthetic-negative, frequency, and multi-property analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 12 newly reports mean ± standard deviation for the fivefold embedding comparison, and Figure 7 adds error bars for label-noise sensitivity without defining their meaning. Existing fold averaging and triplicate laboratory assays remain; increased repetitions of existing experiments are not stated.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover training-data and embedding controls, conditioning-grid errors, range dependence, and label-noise robustness. For example, Table 14 reports 3.2% OmegAMP-classifier positives for PC with SC-derived ranges versus 14.8% with expert ranges. Existing benchmark and laboratory results remain unchanged. The relocated interval-adherence table omits the EV non-AMP reference row.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the cumulative diffusion signal factor from the product of beta_i to the product of (1 - beta_i), updating the forward-diffusion equation accordingly. The remaining mathematical definitions and theoretical arguments are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: controllable AMP generation, biologically informed embeddings, reliable filtering, and a 24/25 experimental hit rate. Additional supporting studies do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning expert-selected conditioning ranges, difficulty combining high charge with high hydrophobicity, embedding informativeness, and weighted-loss robustness to mislabelling. These refine the explanation of the framework; Appendix L's existing applicability and extrapolation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-access URL in the abstract and corrects the AASI scale's expanded name from Surface Area Index to Selectivity Index. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain, as does withholding the synthesized peptide sequences.

R1.justification: v3 adds a Gemini 2.5 citation for its language-assistance disclosure and clarifies that the cited diffusion generators typically lack physicochemical/structural conditional control. The AMP-related bibliography and overall research positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording and terminology corrections, updated author information, new impact/funding/conflict/LLM disclosures, and promotion of the interval-adherence discussion into Section 4.3. The overall narrative and main section order are retained.

P2.justification: The document adopts TMLR typography, headers, expanded front matter, and revised table/figure placement throughout. Three analytical tables and Figures 6–7 are added. v2 Table 11 becomes main-text Table 5 with a revised display; the original five figure images are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new controls and sensitivity studies strengthen validation, while the diffusion correction and code-access information improve clarity and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by reporting weaknesses: I.5's PC-advantage discussion needs qualification because SC scores higher under the OmegAMP classifier (16.4% versus 14.8%), and Figure 7 leaves its error bars undefined.
